runtime.note: A single native binary. The host needs no .NET runtime.

privilege.why: it edits the host firewall, which no unprivileged process can do
privilege.note: This is the one project whose binary and units stay root-owned and whose deploy.sh sudo's those two installs. A root-executed binary an unprivileged user can rewrite is a real escalation path, not a technicality.

anyOf.why: the daemon detects and drives whichever host firewall is present; at least one must exist or it has nothing to configure

system.why: the daemon is socket-activated — the .socket is what gets enabled, the .service is static
editing firewall rules needs CAP_NET_ADMIN, which is why the daemon runs as root

units.note: Enable the .socket, not the .service. SocketGroup=kgsm with mode 0660 is what lets the unprivileged engine reach a root daemon without any further grant — the socket's group IS the access control.
